title: Leveraging In-band Network Telemetry for Automated DDoS Detection in Production Programmable Networks: The AmLight Use Case
problem: In-band Network Telemetry has not been fully realized for real-time network anomaly detection in production systems, and there is a lack of comparative evaluation of INT-based DDoS detection solutions against existing alternatives like sFlow.
motivation: Real-time DDoS detection and mitigation in production networks requires efficient monitoring mechanisms with minimal overhead.
method: The system collects detailed packet information directly from network switches and cards using in-band network telemetry (INT), which adds minimal overhead to the network. This data streams to a central control system that uses machine learning models to analyze it in real-time and detect DDoS attacks. The researchers then compared how well this INT-based detection performs against sFlow (a traditional traffic-sampling approach) in a real production network.
key_novelty: Real-time DDoS detection using in-band network telemetry in production networks, directly compared to sFlow.
contributions: Implementation of real-time INT-based DDoS detection mechanism
Comparative evaluation of INT versus sFlow detection approaches
Integration of machine learning for real-time INT data analysis
Production network deployment in AmLight infrastructure
primary_theme: Real-time DDoS detection using programmable data planes
